solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Eastern Europeans holding power in sports event?

indicators.note: holding means the first letters wrap round and contain the next piece

parts.note: E stands for European, so two of them, plural, give EE
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A group of Eastern European athletes cling to power at some sporting contest.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'Europeans' gives two Es, a doubled abbreviation for a plural.
explanation.definitionFit: This blade is used in one of the three fencing disciplines at the Olympics, hence a sports event, flagged by the question mark.

clue.text: Wizard dispenses with fifty old sheep

indicators.note: dispenses with means the wizard's name does without the following letter

parts.note: Merlin is the wizard of Arthurian legend
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A magician gives up fifty elderly sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a breed of sheep prized for its very fine wool.

clue.text: Parliament's not wanting Liberal to make stand

indicators.note: not wanting means the following letter is unwanted and dropped

parts.note: the Dail is the lower house of the Irish parliament; with the 's it gives DAILS

explanation.surface: A parliament refuses to let the Liberal party take its stand.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dail (Dáil Éireann) is Ireland's lower house; the possessive 's is kept as letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised platform at one end of a hall, where a speaker can stand, is a kind of stand.

clue.text: Alpha male held in very serious respect

parts.note: Alpha is A in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: held in means the male letter is placed inside the word for very serious

parts.note: dire means very serious or dreadful

explanation.surface: An alpha male is held in very serious regard.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold someone in high esteem is to look up to them; both are verbs of regard.

clue.text: Complete rascal not breaking law

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child, a rascal
licit means lawful, so not breaking the law

explanation.surface: An utter rogue who somehow stays within the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complete' looks like an adjective on 'rascal' but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: As in implicit trust or faith: absolute, total, unquestioning.

clue.text: Like Concorde thus carrying posh individual

indicators.note: carrying means the word for thus holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, used to mark a quotation as printed
U means upper-class, posh
a person is an individual

explanation.surface: A posh passenger rides on the luxurious Concorde.
explanation.walkthrough: Concorde was the Anglo-French airliner that flew faster than sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Concorde cruised at twice the speed of sound, so it flew at faster-than-sound speeds.

clue.text: FM broadcast with time for transitory things

indicators.note: broadcast means the two letters are spoken out as their names, giving a sound to spell

parts.note: the letters F and M said out loud as 'eff em'
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: An FM radio programme goes out at a set time, all fleeting stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' looks like a radio word (FM is a radio band) but means the letter names are spoken: 'eff em' becomes EPHEM.
explanation.definitionFit: Items meant to last only a short while, such as tickets and flyers, are short-lived collectables.

clue.text: Wake up in French quarter — outside as it happens

indicators.note: outside means the French word and the quarter go round the next piece

parts.note: en is French for in
N, north, is one of the four quarters of the compass
live means broadcast in real time, as it happens

explanation.surface: Someone wakes up in the French Quarter of a city, outside, as events unfold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French quarter' reads as a district, but splits into 'in French' (EN) and 'quarter' (N).
explanation.definitionFit: To liven up or make lively is to rouse, a transitive sense of wake up.

clue.text: Stupid amount needed for Chinese dish

parts.note: dim means stupid
a sum is an amount

explanation.surface: A foolish quantity is required for a Chinese meal.
explanation.definitionFit: These small steamed or fried Cantonese snacks are served in baskets, a classic Chinese meal.

clue.text: Donnybrook, apparently relaxed, situated in middle?

parts.note: Donnybrook is the setter, who refers to himself as ME
relaxed means laid back; read literally, 'laid back' is the word LAID written backwards, DIAL

explanation.surface: The setter, seemingly calm, sits in the middle of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apparently' warns that 'relaxed' is taken as 'laid back' and then read as an instruction: LAID back.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes something placed at or near the centre, a technical term in anatomy and phonetics.

clue.text: Butchers in group combined talents

indicators.note: in means the butchering word sits inside the word for group

parts.note: a set is a group
butchers means slaughters, kills

explanation.surface: Butchers in a trade group pool their talents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butchers' looks like a plural noun but is a verb, kills.
explanation.definitionFit: The full range of abilities a person brings to a job is their combined talents.

clue.text: Troubles among ladies and gents?

parts.note: in means among
public conveniences are toilets, the ladies and the gents

explanation.surface: Trouble breaks out in the public toilets.
explanation.walkthrough: A public convenience is a British term for a public toilet; the Ladies and the Gents are its two sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Troubles here is a verb, as in it bothers or puts out someone; same plural verb form.

clue.text: Reporter's son grew angry with men

indicators.note: angry suggests the letters are stirred up into a different order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A journalist's son became furious with some men.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Reporter' is 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A gossip who spreads news and rumours is a sort of reporter, though not a professional one.

clue.text: Lowest point for some in a dirigible

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: For some people aboard an airship, this is the low point.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the point directly below an observer, and figuratively the worst moment, the bottom.

clue.text: Get small branch

definitions.meaning: informal British sense: to understand, cotton on
a slender shoot from a tree or shrub

explanation.definitionFit: Colloquially one can catch on to an idea, and a thin shoot of a tree is the other sense.

clue.text: Would Stranglers perform hits with such an instrument?

definitions.text: Would Stranglers perform hits with such an instrument?

parts.words: Would Stranglers perform hits with such an instrument?
parts.note: the Stranglers were a British punk band; a real strangler's tool is a cord or wire used to throttle, so 'instrument' is a strangling device, not a musical one, and 'hits' are killings

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about a band playing its hits on an instrument; really it is about stranglers carrying out hits (contract killings).
explanation.definitionFit: This is a wire or cord used for strangling, the tool of an assassin.

clue.text: Coming in starkers, good way to get attention?

indicators.note: coming in means the abbreviation for good enters the word for naked

parts.note: starkers is British slang for naked, nude

explanation.surface: Arriving naked is a sure way to be noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starkers' is British slang for stark naked.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle poke with the elbow is a way of catching someone's attention.

clue.text: Wanting starter, monster given meat in London district

indicators.note: wanting starter means the monster word loses its first letter

parts.note: a beast is a monster
ham is a cured meat

explanation.surface: A monster skips the first course and is served meat in London.
explanation.walkthrough: East Ham is an area of the London Borough of Newham.
explanation.definitionFit: This area lies in east London, in the borough of Newham.

clue.text: Character is gem but no saint

indicators.note: but no means the gem word is kept but without the saint's letter

parts.note: a stone is a gem

explanation.surface: Someone's nature is a jewel, though no saint.
explanation.definitionFit: The general quality or mood of something, as in the tone of a piece, is its character.

clue.text: Consumer needs analysis, having abused car makers there

indicators.note: abused means the letters are mistreated, knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An investigation into what customers want finds car manufacturers mistreated them.
explanation.definitionFit: Studies of what buyers want and will pay for are surveys of consumer demand.

clue.text: Our leading lady as herself — in rubber?

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen, Britain's leading lady
taken as written
ER again: the Queen herself

explanation.surface: The Queen playing herself in a rubber outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the crossword's usual Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: In British English a rubber is the block used to rub out pencil marks.

clue.text: Have riches perhaps in American vault

parts.note: to vault is to leap or bound

explanation.surface: Perhaps one keeps wealth in a vault in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vault' looks like a bank's strongroom but is a verb, to leap.
explanation.definitionFit: To be plentiful, to exist in great quantity; having riches is one example, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Inappropriate manoeuvring drawn out

indicators.note: manoeuvring means the letters are moved around into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Clumsy scheming that drags on too long.
explanation.definitionFit: Unseemly or unfortunate behaviour is out of place, improper.

clue.text: Sea bass

definitions.meaning: poetic term for the ocean, the main
low in pitch, as a bass voice is

explanation.definitionFit: The ocean is poetically the main, and a low-pitched voice is described as low and resonant.

clue.text: Clean house again

parts.note: over means again, as in do it over

explanation.surface: Clean the house a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the brand name of a vacuum cleaner became a verb for vacuuming a carpet.

clue.text: Champion lacking in height succeeded in love

indicators.note: lacking means the champion word goes without the height letter

parts.note: a hero is a champion
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A short champion has success in romance.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god of desire stands for passion and romantic longing.

clue.text: Headbanging music on Radio Heart

indicators.note: on radio means the word is heard spoken rather than seen written

parts.note: heavy metal is the music fans headbang to

explanation.surface: Heavy rock music played on a station called Radio Heart.
explanation.walkthrough: Heart is also a real UK radio station, which the surface leans on.
explanation.definitionFit: Courage and spirit, as in having the heart to fight on.

clue.text: City where devil misses English in school

indicators.note: in means the shortened devil goes inside the school's name

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

indicators.note: misses means the devil word lacks the English letter

parts.note: a demon is a devil

explanation.surface: A town where a devil skips English lessons at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misses' turns DEMON into DMON, which goes 'in' ETON.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the capital of Alberta in Canada, a large city.
